sentence: This project studies how the motor thalamus and its inputs from the basal ganglia and cerebellum control gait, including in Parkinson's disease mouse models.
This project makes bioinformatic data analysis more available to cancer researchers who use next-generation sequencing.
This project tries to find out which human factors astroviruses use to infect the intestine.
This project studies the molecular mechanisms that control lineage plasticity, a way cancer cells resist therapy, in prostate tumors.
This project tries to find out how lifestyle and genetic factors shape circulating cytokines linked to type 2 diabetes in African-ancestry populations.
This project tests whether matrikine proline-glycine-proline and proteolytic exosomes cause smoke-induced atherosclerosis, using a mouse model.
This project studies what cytochrome b5 reductase 3 does in erythroid cells during erythropoiesis.
This project studies how the lens forms and stays transparent, and builds a web-based tool that helps predict genes linked to cataract.
This project develops gene therapies for Duchenne muscular dystrophy that avoid transgene safety concerns and cause a weaker immune response.
This project uses single-cell RNA sequencing of high-risk neuroblastoma samples to find surface proteoforms that T cell immunotherapy could target.
This project studies how DNA variation relates to many aspects of human musicality.
This project offers microscopy resources, including fluorescence and electron microscopy, along with advice on experimental design and data analysis.
This project receives, processes and stores tissues from patients with myeloproliferative neoplasms and shares them with researchers.
This project tests engineered tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes combined with drugs against glioblastoma and studies effects on neurons, astrocytes and oligodendrocytes.
This project uses inner ear stem cells and induced otic progenitors to find the pathways and genes that give otic progenitors their stem cell potential.
This project uses machine learning on drug seizure data and county-level overdose mortality data to spot changes in the illicit drug supply.
This project studies how glutamate receptors work, including their structure, genetic variation linked to rare disease, and their role in synaptic transmission.
This project tests a molecular platform with a built-in microbial sequence that aims to help the immune system fight head and neck cancer.
This project uses repeated neuropsychological testing, blood biomarkers and advanced imaging to study neurologic and mental health complications after COVID-19 infection.
This project uses a microscope that can visualize phase-separated cell structures in living cells to study phase separation biology.
